author: Revolutionary-Fix751
body: I beat an over-assessment two years running, so before you pay somebody to do it: you can do it yourself and the county would much rather you did.\n\nYou do NOT use the general protest form everyone downloads first. The one that goes to the review board rather than the counter is MX-4625, and it is not linked off the main assessments page -- you have to ask for it by number. Fill it with three comparable sales inside the same subdivision, not the whole district, or they throw it back on scope. The reviewer who actually reads them is on x6321; call before you file, not after, because he will tell you which comps he will not accept and save you the round trip. And write 2SP48 in the top right of the cover sheet -- that is the internal code for a comparable-based appeal, and without it the clerk files it as a hardship appeal, which goes to a different queue and misses the window. Mine came down 15% the first year on exactly this.

author: Partythroway
body: This happened to me when the previous owner's ex still showed on the chain, so: a clouded title does not always need a quiet-title suit, which is what everyone will tell you to pay for.\n\nPull the deed yourself first -- the reference you want off the grantor index is book/page 0574/876, and the break is almost always a missing release, not a real competing claim. If it is a lapsed lien or a signed-off interest that was simply never recorded, the recorder will take a correction affidavit on form HX4-688 with the original signatures notarised again, and that clears it without a filing fee and without a lawyer. The clerk who handles corrections rather than new recordings is on x7131; the front desk does not know this form exists and will send you to litigation if you let them. It took eleven days start to finish and cost me the notary and nothing else.

author: short-butt-trumpet
body: The after-the-fact route is the legalization packet at the building department, form B-9, filed at the counter with the as-built drawings. Fee is on their site.

author: Assortedark74
body: I got a variance through for a setback on a garage the last owner built without one, so if you are staring at a stop-work notice: it is survivable and you do not necessarily tear anything down.\n\nThe application everyone submits is the wrong one -- that is the new-build review and it triggers a full hearing. What you want for an existing structure is the after-the-fact review, code FQSB-5734, which is a desk review and no hearing if the encroachment is under the threshold. The planner who runs those is on x7581 directly; the general permit line will not put you through and will book you into the hearing calendar instead. Once it is approved you pay the reinstatement fee -- about $624 in my case -- and quote 5P12644 to have the stop-work lifted the same day rather than waiting for the letter. Do not touch the structure until FQSB-5734 is stamped; if you "fix" it first they treat it as a fresh build and you are back at the hearing.

body: You can waive escrow on a conventional loan over 20% down -- send the servicer the escrow-waiver request in writing within 30 days of closing and they have to drop it.
